what: Starbucks runs and licenses coffeehouses in 91 markets. It roasts its own coffee, sells drinks and food in its own stores and through licensed outlets, and sells packaged coffee in supermarkets through a partnership with Nestlé.
customers: Consumers buying coffee and food in stores and through its app; licensees and grocery buyers of packaged products.
money: company-operated and licensed stores in the US and Canada
stores worldwide, with China the largest and most contested market
packaged coffee and ready-to-drink products sold through Nestlé and partners
moat: A brand that supports premium prices, dense store locations, and a loyalty app that holds customer balances and drives repeat visits.
risks: US same-store sales have been weak and the turnaround is taking time
Chinese competitors undercut it heavily on price
Labour costs and unionisation efforts raise store expenses
Profit margins have fallen while the company reinvests in stores and staff
opportunities: The current turnaround is simplifying the menu and cutting waiting times, which can restore traffic
Store growth continues in international markets
Channel Development earns high margins with little capital
watch: US same-store transactions, not just the ticket size, and the China business after the local partnership deal.
